`.python-version` and `requires-python` aren't really interchangeable here. `.python-version` tells uv which interpreter to pick at dev time. `requires-python` is the range the resolver uses to decide which package versions are compatible, and it ends up encoded in `uv.lock`. Without it, uv has to guess a default from whatever interpreter is active, which is what the warning is flagging (see `crates/uv/src/commands/project/lock.rs` around the `No \`requires-python\`` branch). Silencing it when `.python-version` is present would hide that, because `.python-version` can be a full pin like `3.12.4`, which isn't the same thing as a supported range.

Subject to correction, I believe the issue you’re describing, needing project.name and project.version just to declare a supported Python range, is tracked in #10204, which is still marked as needs-design.

Until something like that is addressed, the intended approach is to include a [project] table with placeholder name and version values in order to set requires-python for a non-package project.
